stories.headline: Pakistan holds nationwide Marka-e-Haq first anniversary ceremonies; Munir warns of consequences, PM declares national day
stories.summary: Pakistan marked the first anniversary of its declared victory in the May 2025 four-day conflict with India with ceremonies at GHQ, the Pakistan Monument, Wagah Border, and Karachi. CDF Asim Munir addressed the GHQ ceremony, calling the conflict a 'battle between two ideologies,' warning of 'far-reaching and painful consequences' for any future aggression, highlighting military modernisation including new Rocket Force and Hangor-class submarines, and urging Afghanistan to deny sanctuary to TTP. PM Shehbaz Sharif declared May 10 as 'Marka-e-Haq Day,' said Pakistan's response forced India to seek a ceasefire, and President Zardari praised Munir's leadership. Maryam Nawaz presided at Wagah; Bilawal Bhutto led PPP events in Karachi and Sindh.

stories.headline: Iran transmits response to US peace proposal via Pakistan; Trump immediately rejects it as 'totally unacceptable'
stories.summary: Iran submitted its response to the latest US proposal to end the Middle East war to Pakistani mediators on Sunday, May 10; PM Shehbaz Sharif publicly confirmed receipt, saying CDF Asim Munir had informed him, and adding that the response focused on permanently ending the conflict. President Trump almost immediately rejected it as 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE.' Pakistan has been conducting 'neutral mediation' between Washington and Tehran since hosting 21-hour Islamabad talks in mid-April; Munir separately reiterated Islamabad's commitment to the mediation effort and held phone calls with his Qatari counterpart. The story attracted global wire pickup across dozens of international outlets due to the active Iran-US conflict context.

stories.headline: Suicide car bombing and ambush in Bannu kills 14-15 police officers; TTP splinter group claims responsibility
stories.summary: Late Saturday night (May 9), militants detonated an explosives-laden vehicle at the Fatehkhel police checkpoint in Bannu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, followed by an armed ambush on responders that raised the death toll to at least 15 police officers. A self-proclaimed TTP splinter group, Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, claimed responsibility; authorities accused it of being a TTP front. PM Shehbaz condemned the attack in a call with KP CM Sohail Afridi; President Zardari also issued condolences.

stories.headline: ISPR holds Marka-e-Haq anniversary press conference; DG ISPR's 'why English?' remark goes viral
stories.summary: DG ISPR Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry held a press conference on May 7-8 marking the first anniversary of Marka-e-Haq, outlining ten strategic consequences of the conflict, claiming Pakistan defeated India 'across all domains,' and declaring Pakistan is 'preparing for the future war.' His aside questioning why Indian Army officers addressed their anniversary press conference in English went viral on social media and in Indian media, with even Pakistani critics mocking the remark. ISPR also released a teaser for a new patriotic song 'Lalkar' and a documentary marking the anniversary.

stories.headline: Imran Khan's Al Qadir Trust appeal adjourned; PTI demands May 9 judicial commission and Imran's release
stories.summary: The Islamabad High Court adjourned the main appeal hearing in Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi's £190 million Al Qadir Trust corruption case to May 20, after Khan's counsel requested more time. Separately, the IHC earlier in the week rejected petitions seeking suspension of their sentences. PTI simultaneously marked the third anniversary of Imran's May 9, 2023 arrest by demanding an independent judicial commission to probe the events, the release of CCTV footage, and Imran and Bushra's immediate release. PTI also walked out of the Senate over concerns about Bushra's undisclosed hospital visit for eye treatment.

stories.headline: Munir's domestic power consolidation draws international analytical attention
stories.summary: Several analytical pieces this week — including from Carnegie Endowment — examined how CDF Asim Munir has steadily consolidated control over Pakistan's political, economic, and institutional framework over three years, formalising the military's dominant role. The Carnegie report noted the military's gamble on international legitimacy to compensate for domestic governance failures. Indian and other regional outlets picked up these analyses in the context of the Marka-e-Haq anniversary.

stories.headline: Former Pentagon official Michael Rubin publishes provocative op-ed calling Pakistan a strategic tool 'to use and discard'
stories.summary: Michael Rubin, a former US Pentagon official, published an op-ed calling Pakistan an unreliable partner that Washington historically uses and discards; he used vulgar language to describe the Pakistan-US relationship and called Munir 'just the latest pimp,' criticising Trump for honouring Munir despite Pakistan's record of harbouring terrorists. The piece was widely picked up by Indian and American outlets, with some framing it as a warning that Pakistan should not expect lasting US strategic favour from its Iran mediation role.

stories.headline: China confirms it provided on-site military technical assistance to Pakistan during May 2025 India conflict
stories.summary: South China Morning Post reported that China officially confirmed for the first time that it provided on-site technical support to Pakistan's air force during the four-day 2025 conflict with India, with Chinese aerospace engineer Zhang Heng revealing the involvement in a CCTV interview. This was the first public acknowledgment of direct Chinese personnel involvement. Indian media gave the story prominent coverage on the Marka-e-Haq anniversary week.

stories.headline: Pakistan energy minister calls himself 'ordinary worker' of CDF Munir, sparking viral backlash over military's civilian dominance
stories.summary: Federal Energy Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik, a close aide to PM Shehbaz, described himself at a press conference as 'an ordinary worker of Field Marshal Asim Munir,' drawing widespread ridicule on social media and commentary arguing the remark exposed the military's expanding grip over civilian politics. The incident was covered in Indian and Pakistani media as a telling sign of the military-civilian power imbalance.

stories.headline: Pakistan military modernisation: FATAH-3 supersonic missile unveiled and post-conflict capability rebuilding analysed
stories.summary: Pakistan's Army Rocket Force Command publicly unveiled the FATAH-3 supersonic cruise missile, widely believed to be based on China's HD-1 system, in conjunction with the Marka-e-Haq anniversary. Defence analysts at Quwa and Defence Security Asia noted that Pakistan has systematically built an independent, multi-domain precision-strike architecture since the 2025 conflict, including new rocket force divisions and UAV units. Munir also referenced the Hangor-class submarines and the Rocket Force in his GHQ speech.

stories.headline: PML-N and PPP prepare for AJK and Gilgit-Baltistan elections; Nawaz chairs candidate-selection meetings
stories.summary: Nawaz Sharif chaired PML-N's Azad Jammu and Kashmir Parliamentary Board meeting to finalise candidates for upcoming AJK elections and announced he would personally campaign in mid-June. PML-N separately released its candidate list for 19 of 24 Gilgit-Baltistan seats. PPP and JUI-F announced an electoral alliance for AJK. An AJK cabinet minister was also reportedly in talks to defect to PML-N.
